parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two capacitors, of capacitances *C*₁ and *C*₂, are connected in parallel to a power supply of electromotive force (e.m.f.) *E*, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Show that the combined capacitance *C*ₜ of the two capacitors is given by

*C*ₜ = *C*₁ + *C*₂

Explain your reasoning. You may draw on Fig. 5.1 if you wish.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
Two capacitors, of capacitances 22 μF and 47 μF, and a resistor of resistance 2.7 MΩ, are connected into the circuit of Fig. 5.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The battery has an e.m.f. of 12 V.
parts.text: Show that the combined capacitance of the two capacitors is 15 μF.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The two-way switch S is initially at position X, so that the capacitors are fully charged.

Use the information in (c)(i) to calculate the total energy stored in the two capacitors.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The two-way switch is now moved to position Y.

Determine the time taken for the potential difference (p.d.) across the 22 μF capacitor to become 6.0 V.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A circuit diagram shows two capacitors C₁ and C₂ connected in parallel with a power supply E.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
